chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to judge with one witness along with an oath from the owner of the right.

key_terms.شَاهِد: Witness (shahid) — a qualified legal witness whose testimony is accepted in court
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحَقّ: Owner of the right — the plaintiff or claimant who asserts a legal right or claim
key_terms.يَقْضِي: He judged/ruled — refers to the Prophet's judicial practice and precedent-setting decisions
key_terms.يَمِين: Oath (yamin) — a sworn statement made by the claimant to supplement insufficient witness testimony

ai.seo_question: Can a judge rule based on one witness and an oath in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) established the legal practice of accepting judgment based on a single witness combined with an oath (yamin) from the claimant. This ruling addresses a situation where a plaintiff has only one witness but cannot produce the standard two required by Islamic law; in such cases, the claimant may supplement their single witness with their own sworn oath. This principle was well-established in early Islamic jurisprudence as a means of ensuring access to justice when full witness requirements could not be met.
